problem: Extreme quantization in LLMs requires balancing ultra-low bit efficiency with model performance, but residual binarization suffers from pathological feature co-adaptation across parallel paths.
approach: RaBiT enforces a residual hierarchy during Quantization-Aware Training by sequentially deriving each binary path from a shared full-precision weight, ensuring each path corrects its predecessor's error, stabilized by robust initialization.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art 2-bit accuracy while rivals hardware-intensive Vector Quantization and delivers 4.49x inference speedup on RTX 4090.

problem: Motion planning struggles to unify deep learning-based generative priors with model-based planning's flexibility and domain knowledge incorporation.
approach: Learns an autoencoder with hierarchically ordered discrete-valued tokens in latent space, then performs motion planning via direct search in the compressed latent space to optimize arbitrary test-time objectives.
contribution: Enables closed-loop motion planning and multi-agent scenario synthesis on nuPlan and Waymo Open Motion Dataset without task-specific training.

problem: Reliable uncertainty quantification for causal effects as entire functions rather than scalar estimands remains challenging, especially with pathological prior constructions for RKHS functions.
approach: GP-based approach using interventional functions as inner products of observational functions in RKHS, with appropriate GP priors for posteriors inferred from observational data.
contribution: Yields closed-form posterior moments and tractable training/inference while improving uncertainty quantification across synthetic benchmarks, Bayesian optimization tasks, and large-scale real data.

problem: Text-to-video diffusion transformers encode semantic information unevenly across depth, limiting effective concept erasure where target concepts and non-target signals remain entangled outside optimal representational depths.
approach: CLEAR identifies representational depths where concept-non-target separation emerges naturally, then operationalizes layer selection as optimization over separability rather than using layer-agnostic or heuristic choices.
contribution: Enforcing concept-layer alignment leads to more precise concept suppression while preserving generative quality on large-scale text-to-video models.

problem: Users face overwhelming choices selecting appropriate LLMs from a rapidly growing pool with distinct latent properties that are often opaque and difficult to articulate.
approach: Interaction-efficient active learning using dueling bandits to iteratively select LLM pairs, collect user feedback, and update beliefs about user preferences via belief-aware upper confidence bound strategy.
contribution: Efficiently matches users to LLMs under cost and time budgets with lower cost than existing multi-LLM collaboration methods, verified through diverse experiments and human studies.

problem: Forecasting urban phenomena requires effective integration of geospatial data, but current methods either use task-specific models or generic models with limited multimodal fusion capabilities.
approach: UrbanFusion uses modality-specific encoders for street view, remote sensing, maps, and POIs, integrating them via Transformer-based fusion module to learn unified spatial representations.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art GeoAI models on 41 tasks across 56 cities, generalizes to unseen regions, and flexibly utilizes any subset of available modalities at inference.

problem: Video generative models struggle to generalize to unconventional camera motions crucial for artistic videos due to insufficient training data with intended uncommon camera motions.
approach: VividCam learns complex camera motions from synthetic videos via diffusion models using multiple disentanglement strategies that isolate camera motion learning from synthetic appearance artifacts.
contribution: Synthesizes precisely controlled unconventional camera motions using simple low-poly synthetic data, reducing reliance on collecting realistic training videos.

problem: GNN-based recommendation systems process graph structural information and LLM-derived semantic knowledge separately, creating a supervisory gap between collaborative filtering and semantic relevance.
approach: CCLRec identifies structural-semantic consensus by computing intersection between a node's structural neighbors and semantically similar items, then applies contrastive learning on these high-confidence consensus pairs.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art on multiple public recommendation benchmarks by centering learning on consensus features and weight-aware reinforcement.

problem: Conformal Prediction methods generate prediction sets guaranteed to include true labels but often contain too many classes, particularly problematic when classes can be grouped by shared downstream actions.
approach: Augments CP score functions with terms penalizing out-of-group errors, then leverages class-similarity factors to reduce average set size without requiring explicit human semantic partitions.
contribution: Consistently enhances CP methods across prominent approaches and datasets, reducing mean accuracy variance 3x with minimal performance decrease, and can work without manual class partitions.

problem: The Mamba model's in-context learning capabilities and training dynamics remain theoretically opaque, especially regarding robustness to outliers compared to Transformers.
approach: Provides first theoretical analysis of one-layer Mamba's training dynamics, showing it uses linear attention to select informative context and nonlinear gating to suppress outlier influence.
contribution: Demonstrates Mamba maintains accurate predictions even when outlier proportion exceeds Transformer thresholds, supported by empirical verification on binary classification.

problem: Accelerating optimal transport while respecting computational constraints remains challenging, particularly when exploiting intrinsic problem structure like symmetries.
approach: Recovers orbit decomposition and associated algebra from cost matrix to reduce original transport problem to substantially smaller one on orbit space, developing efficient solvers for linear and entropy-regularized OT.
contribution: First systematic incorporation of symmetry groups into optimal transport, providing theoretical framework and practical speedups on synthetic, real-world image, and molecular graph data.

problem: Traditional comorbidity scores are mortality-centric and use linear rule-based structures that cannot capture nonlinear, outcome-specific risk relationships.
approach: MLCI maps diagnosis codes to scalar by maximizing normalized Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion between learned score and multiple clinical outcomes.
contribution: Outperforms strong baselines across multiple evaluation metrics on EHR datasets, capturing nonlinear risk-outcome dependence across multiple outcomes.

problem: Visual Autoregressive models suffer from sharply increased computational complexity at large-scale steps, limiting practical applicability despite their high-quality generation.
approach: FasterVAR identifies that early stages preserve semantic structure (should remain intact) while later stages refine details (can be pruned), exploiting this stage-aware insight with semantic irrelevance and low-rank properties.
contribution: Achieves up to 3.4x speedup with almost no performance loss, consistently outperforming acceleration baselines on VAR models.

problem: Language models exhibit position-bias and label-bias on multiple-choice question benchmarks, using answer position or label distributions rather than semantic reasoning.
approach: ABCD proposes bias-reduced evaluation by replacing labels with uniform unordered ones and requiring full answer presentation, using similarity models to enhance robustness.
contribution: Reduces mean accuracy variance 3x across benchmarks and models with minimal performance decrease, exposing LLM capabilities under reduced evaluation artifacts.

problem: Circuit analysis typically explains single target-conditioned outputs, obscuring heterogeneity across a model's full continuation distribution and mechanistic factors.
approach: Distribution-level unsupervised feature discovery clusters continuations using semantic content and mechanistic attributions without manual target specification, optimizing rate-distortion over these two views.
contribution: Discovers continuation modes missed by single-view baselines with interventional evidence that cluster signatures correspond to actionable mechanistic factors.

problem: Extending conformal prediction to vector-valued outputs requires capturing joint multivariate dependencies, but scalar aggregation discards geometry while optimal transport approaches are computationally demanding.
approach: GCQR and GRCP use geometric quantiles and spatial ranks for multivariate uncertainty, with scalable learning via partially input-convex neural networks.
contribution: Attain near-nominal coverage with consistently tighter prediction regions than baselines on multi-target regression and multi-class classification.

problem: Features from different pretrained models exhibit distinct distributions, making it challenging to learn invariant representations from unlabeled data across heterogeneous views in unsupervised transfer.
approach: MSRL exploits self-representation property of features across views, using information-passing mechanism and assignment probability distribution consistency to enforce invariance.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches with theoretical analysis of assignment distribution consistency and incremental views.

problem: Understanding how neural networks generalize (mechanistic interpretability) focuses on reverse-engineering internal structure, but determining what training data produces desired generalization remains unexplored.
approach: Patterning inverts the linear response of susceptibilities to determine data interventions steering models toward target internal configurations.
contribution: Demonstrates re-weighting training data can accelerate/delay structure formation like induction circuits, and select which algorithm the model learns by targeting local learning coefficients.

problem: Language modeling is ill-posed with multiple plausible continuations from context, but standard next-token prediction cannot handle this inherent ambiguity.
approach: LoRA-MCL extends next-token prediction with Multiple Choice Learning and winner-takes-all loss via Low-Rank Adaptation to efficiently decode diverse continuations.
contribution: Achieves high diversity and relevance in generated outputs on audio/visual captioning and machine translation, with released code for wide model applicability.

problem: Users need cost-efficient access to powerful LLMs, but cloud-hosted LLMs are expensive while locally deployed small models lack capability for complex tasks.
approach: Selective Deferred Routing routes requests between local SLMs and remote LLMs based on a lightweight decision module using semantic representations and prediction uncertainty.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing multi-LLM collaboration methods across diverse models and datasets under various cost-performance trade-offs.

problem: LLMs encounter distribution shifts during real-world deployment causing performance degradation, and test-time learning via entropy minimization faces error propagation and model collapse.
approach: FG-TTL learns selectively from high-gain tokens that reduce uncertainty in subsequent generation, using Future-Gain metric and Risk-Aware Adaptation with adaptive temperature scaling.
contribution: Achieves best average performance across six benchmarks and three LLM backbones by concentrating learning on informative positions.

problem: Neural scaling laws relate loss to model size but depth and width contributions differ, and deeper LLMs may not benefit from compositional learning.
approach: Quantifies depth effects via LLM and toy network analysis, finding loss scales inversely with depth due to functionally similar layers providing ensemble averaging rather than compositional learning.
contribution: Shows inverse depth scaling in LLMs suggests inefficient yet robust regime, potentially requiring architectural innovations for compositional depth use.

problem: New AI accelerators with novel instruction sets require manual kernel development, slowing hardware adoption, but it remains unclear if agentic LLMs can generate efficient kernels for emerging hardware.
approach: KernelCraft evaluates LLM agents' kernel generation via function-calling feedback-driven workflow, testing across three emerging accelerators on 20+ ML tasks with five configurations each.
contribution: Demonstrates leading reasoning models generate functionally correct kernels for unseen ISAs within refinement steps and produce optimized kernels matching compiler baselines.

problem: Multi-objective protein design requires adapting to shifting targets without retraining, but test-time diffusion methods learn ineffectively from history, over-rely on successes, and struggle balancing competing objectives.
approach: MoMST develops memory bank from historical iterations, extracts preference signals from both successful and failed cases via self-contrastive learning, and applies Pareto alignment for objective balance.
contribution: Achieves remarkable performance on single and complex multi-objective protein design tasks with code availability.

problem: Equilibrium computation in imperfect-recall extensive-form games is provably hard and lacks scalable algorithmic approaches.
approach: Proposes sum-of-squares hierarchies over behavioral strategies for ex-ante optimal strategies in single-player and Nash equilibria in multi-player imperfect-recall games.
contribution: Proves asymptotic convergence with finite convergence under genericity, and identifies (SOS)-concave/(SOS)-monotone classes with first-level convergence via single SDP.

problem: Vision-Language Models perform well on commonsense reasoning but struggle with visual spatial reasoning without relying on extra 3D priors that degrade general capabilities.
approach: SpatioLM designs parameter-efficient non-invasive spatio-vision module eliciting spatial knowledge inherent in VLMs, using pseudo depth and camera information as supervision.
contribution: Achieves significant improvements across spatial and general tasks, scoring 71.6 on VSI-Bench (first model exceeding 70) and transfers to embodied manipulation.

problem: Pretraining optimizers tune for strongest base models but neglect geometry controlling capability survival through post-training and quantization.
approach: Studies three approaches biasing toward flatter minima: Sharpness-Aware Minimization, large learning rates, and shortened annealing, showing they reduce forgetting during post-training.
contribution: Across 20M-150M models, flat-minima approaches reduce forgetting up to 80% after post-training, with SAM mid-training reducing forgetting 31% after MetaMath and 40% after quantization at scale.

problem: Agentic LLMs assume fixed tool inventories limiting adaptability to new or evolving toolsets during reasoning.
approach: AutoTool trains agents with dynamic tool-selection via dual-phase optimization: SFT/RL trajectory stabilization plus KL-regularized Plackett-Luce ranking for tool selection.
contribution: On 200k dataset with 1000+ tools and 100+ tasks, AutoTool with fewer parameters consistently outperforms advanced agents, averaging 6.4% gains in math/science, 4.5% in QA, 7.7% in code, 6.9% in multimodal.

problem: Existing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures regularize toward isotropic Gaussian distributions, failing to capture sparsity observed in efficient biological representations.
approach: Rectified LpJEPA introduces Rectified Distribution Matching Regularization matching representations to Rectified Generalized Gaussian distribution enabling explicit sparsity control.
contribution: Learns sparse non-negative representations with favorable sparsity-performance tradeoffs and competitive downstream performance on image classification.

problem: Normalization Equivariance improves robustness to distribution shift but existing methods constrain all layers to NE-compatible operations, excluding standard components and adding runtime cost.
approach: Wrapped Normalization Equivariance uses parameter-free wrapper normalizing input, applying any backbone, denormalizing output, exactly parameterizing NE function class.
contribution: Wrapping CNNs and Transformers improves blind denoising robustness under noise-level mismatch with no GPU overhead, while architectural baselines are up to 1.6x slower.

problem: World-model-based imagination for robotic manipulation supports either image-based forecasting or partial 3D geometry, limiting complete 4D scene dynamics prediction.
approach: MVISTA-4D enables arbitrary-view RGBD generation from single-view observation through cross-view/cross-modality fusion, addressing action inference via test-time optimization through generative model.
contribution: Strong performance on both 4D scene generation and downstream manipulation across three datasets with practical insights from ablations.

problem: Neural Tangent Kernel framework fails to depict foundation model finetuning as it neglects preconditioning effects of adaptive gradients.
approach: Optimizer Aware Kernel incorporates optimizer influence via preconditioner estimation and derives error bounds explaining kernel regime collapse from cumulative training effects and task discrepancy.
contribution: Shows effectiveness of OAK method across architectures and justifies when/why kernel regime fails during finetuning.

problem: Score-based diffusion models struggle to generate clean samples when training data comes from noisy version of target distribution.
approach: MAD uses manifold hypothesis motivating extended score concept distinguishing on-manifold from off-manifold variation, reducing small variations to zero while preserving large relevant variations.
contribution: Efficiently implementable modification improves noiseless sample generation on toy, synthetic, and real data.

problem: Constraint-based causal discovery via conditional independence tests fails as conditioning sets grow, particularly in hub-dominated graphs.
approach: OCMB treats conditioning-set dimensionality as first-class constraint via two-stage approach: lightweight global ordering for priors, then local Markov blanket validation within small ordering-constrained sets.
contribution: Significantly improves precision and robustness in high-dimensional regimes where conventional CI-based approaches fail.

problem: Processing worldwide OpenStreetMap data is computationally intensive with difficult unification for benchmarking, and billion-scale road networks remain underexplored for model scalability.
approach: OSM+ uses distributed cloud computing with 5,000 cores to process OSM data and release billion-vertex structured road network graph with spatial query interface.
contribution: Enables broader spatial coverage with 31-city traffic prediction benchmark scaling from hundreds to thousands of intersections, plus six-city policy control at thousand-scale multi-agent coordination.

problem: Existing video diffusion models are constrained by rigid inference paradigms: bidirectional excels at coherence but slow, autoregressive efficient but lacks consistency and suffers exposure bias.
approach: Flex-Forcing uses flexible chunking over temporal axis and denoising steps enabling bidirectional inference across chunks for planning while generating autoregressively within chunks.
contribution: Achieves consistently better video quality and long-video stability than baselines with rigid schedules while offering faster inference.

problem: Tokenization introduces distortion into LLM generations (Prompt Boundary Problem) affecting code/non-English where tokens misalign with syntactic boundaries.
approach: Converts any autoregressive LM with BPE tokenizer into character/byte-level LM at inference via efficient method, also enabling vocabulary unification and ensemble across models.
contribution: Solves PBP and enables LLM ensemble/post-training transfer with different tokenizers.

problem: Boosting algorithms combining weak learners have various implementations with suboptimal runtimes.
approach: QuantumBoost uses quantum algorithm for approximate Bregman projections with lazy projection strategy where projections occur infrequently.
contribution: Achieves best known runtime for boosting, first successful lazy projection strategy in boosting context.

problem: GP bandit algorithms have dimension-dependent logarithmic factor gaps between upper and lower regret bounds for squared exponential kernels.
approach: Studies algorithm-independent worst-case lower bounds for SE kernel GP bandits on hyperspherical domain.
contribution: Shows any algorithm suffers Omega(sqrt(T(ln T)^d(ln ln T)^-d)) cumulative regret and improves information gain upper bounds to O((ln T)^(d+1)(ln ln T)^-d), achieving near-optimality.

problem: Hypergraph contrastive learning assumes nodes within hyperedges are semantically homogeneous, but real hypergraphs contain heterogeneous interactions causing feature contamination.
approach: H2CL estimates node-hyperedge heterogeneity to guide Heterogeneity-Aware View Generator for cleaner views and Encoder that reweights message propagation dynamically.
contribution: Achieves competitive/superior performance compared to baselines, remains robust under structural noise, learns reweighting patterns reducing heterogeneity.
